speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To narrow down the cause, have you been in close contact with anyone who has a similar rash or known infection recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area following a viral prodrome is very specific. Given your age and these symptoms, have your joints, ankles, or wrists become swollen or painful recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_Rash_Photograph

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC: Normal, Hemoglobin: Normal, Platelets: Slightly elevated; Skin_Rash_Photograph: Lacy, reticular rash noted on the trunk and extremities. Facial rash present but sparing the perioral area. Rash is slightly raised but not accompanied by significant warmth or tenderness.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.
